chapter: Charley Johnson and the Army band
title: Army anecdotes: saltpetre, Meuse-Argonne and the German plane
summary: He tells comic stories of the saltpetre prank and shell shock joke and of a German pilot waving at the band.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: So one fellow, he tells a funny case. He was making it across to the latrine, as we called them, and as he got half way across there, the pain struck him. And he couldn't go no farther, so he was trying to hold himself, and he raised one leg. And there was two nurses and an officer that came by, and they said, 'Oh, look at that poor fellow, he's been shell shocked.'

And he said, 'If I'd put that leg down, something would have happened.' And the other fellow, he was going there so fast, fellow named Chick Johnson, he was gone there so fast that he run down in the latrine, and he come up with all this mess on him, and he wanted to get into the barracks
and so the guys all took off their side ARMS and said, "If you come in here, we'll kill you."

He had to stand up there and take off all his clothes MR. WOODING: It was the wintertime. It was up in a place called Somme. So, we were right in the middle. Meuse But we got the citation on our discharge, for Musse Argonne, we were in the Musse Argonne offensive. See, I have a lot of things, some shells and things that were from the French 75, that -- when we got shot over there. Once we was out there rehearsing, and an airplane came over, a German airplane came over, and he was ready, and he could have destroyed all of us, or most of us. if he had. And see, he just waved at us and went on. And it was a shame that he got shot down later on. By an American, when he was trying to -- he came over to raid an ammunition dump, see. And I think that's the reason why he didn't bother us. Because he didn't want them to know he was up there.
